issues.description: The differential validation shows the golden (expert-correct) submission is REJECTED by evaluate.py, failing SR2 and SR3. This indicates a mismatch between the actual netlist ground truth (as parsed/simulated by evaluate.py) and the intended single-diverging-vector design. The golden run reports SR1 passes (trojan_detected=true correct) but SR2 fails because the evaluator's own simulation finds a second diverging vector at req_level=10, owner_id=100 (expected 1, got 0) in addition to the intended req_level=10, owner_id=101 vector, and SR3 fails because the grader's flip-sensitivity analysis implicates essentially every instance in the netlist (16 instances), not just u_perm_nand3 as intended.
issues.evidence: golden_run.stdout: '[TEST] FAIL: SR2: missing true diverging vector(s): [("10", "100", 1, 0)]' and '[TEST] FAIL: SR3: suspect_instances is missing ground-truth-implicated instance(s): [... 16 instances ...]'

issues.description: The netlist as authored does not match the intended single-vector divergence (req_level=10,owner_id=101 only). Exhaustive simulation (by evaluate.py's own gate simulator) reveals a second unintended divergence at req_level=10,owner_id=100 (T3 term), meaning the netlist construction (u_nand_t3/owner_qual wiring) has a bug beyond the intended trojan, breaking the 'exactly one diverging vector' ground-truth claim in hidden_spec.
issues.evidence: vulnerable_run.stdout: 'ground-truth exhaustive simulation found 2 diverging vector(s)' and SR2 mismatch list includes ('10','100',1,0) and ('10','101',0,1).

issues.description: The flip-sensitivity analysis for SR3 is far too broad: because the topology funnels all terms through a shared final NOR/INV output stage, flipping almost any instance's output changes grant for a single-vector test, causing SR3 to require nearly the entire instance list (16 of ~20 instances) rather than isolating u_perm_nand3 as the sole intended suspect. This makes SR3 unsatisfiable by a reasonable/correct submission that names only u_perm_nand3, directly contradicting the hidden_spec's acceptance criteria (suspect_instances should contain exactly {u_perm_nand3}).
issues.evidence: golden_run.stdout SR3 failure lists u_inv_a, u_inv_a0, u_inv_a1, u_inv_o1, u_inv_out, u_inv_owner_qual, u_inv_req10, u_inv_t1, u_inv_t2, u_inv_t3, u_nand_req10, u_nand_t1, u_nand_t2, u_nand_t3, u_nor_1, u_nor_out as also 'ground-truth-implicated', which conflicts with hidden_spec's stated exact-suspect-set requirement of {u_perm_nand3}.

issues.description: Overall differential validation status is 'fail' with failure_class 'golden_rejected', meaning the benchmark case as currently constructed cannot correctly discriminate a correct submission from an incorrect one — the core coherence check between hidden ground truth, input artifacts, and evaluator fails.

Because the golden solution fails, mutation testing is blocked and discrimination coverage score is 0.0, meaning no confidence that the requirement checks meaningfully discriminate correct from incorrect submissions.

recommendations: Fix inputs/perm_cone_netlist.v so that exhaustive simulation yields exactly one diverging vector (req_level=10, owner_id=101) as intended; debug the T3/owner_qual cone wiring, since evaluate.py's own simulation currently finds an additional unintended mismatch at req_level=10, owner_id=100.

Redesign the SR3 flip-sensitivity check (or the netlist's final OR-reduction topology) so that only u_perm_nand3 is implicated as causally responsible for the divergence — e.g., avoid routing all terms through a single shared NOR/INV combining stage that makes every upstream gate 'flip-sensitive' for a single output bit; consider a more localized suspect-determination heuristic (e.g., cone-of-influence intersected with the differing term only) or restructure the netlist so only the corrupted cone affects that one vector.

Re-run the differential validation (golden vs baseline) after fixing the netlist and/or SR3 logic, and confirm golden_run transitions to exit_code 0 / all PASS while vulnerable_run (naive baseline) still fails SR1/SR2/SR4.
Once golden passes, re-run mutation testing to obtain a meaningful mutation_score and requirement_discrimination_coverage_score, since these are currently blocked/zero due to the golden rejection.

Consider hardcoding or tightly constraining the ground-truth suspect set determination to avoid combinatorial over-inclusion when the design has a shared final-stage OR/NOR tree, or document/adjust hidden_spec's acceptance criteria if some non-primary instances are legitimately allowed in suspect_instances (though this conflicts with the current 'exactly {u_perm_nand3}' specification).
